parts.text: The IGCSE class is determining the internal volume of a test-tube using two displacement methods. The apparatus used is shown in Figs. 5.1, 5.2 and 5.3. Fig. 5.1 Fig. 5.2

parts.label: i
parts.text: (a) (i) Fig. 5.1 shows water in a measuring cylinder. Record the volume V 1 of the water. V 1 = ................................................. [1]

parts.label: ii
parts.text: (ii) On Fig. 5.1, show clearly the line of sight that you would use to obtain an accurate volume reading. [2]

parts.label: i
parts.text: (b) (i) A student lowers a test-tube, closed end first, into the water in the measuring cylinder and pushes the tube down until it is filled with water. From Fig. 5.2, record the new water level V 2 . V 2 = ......................................................

parts.label: ii
parts.text: (ii) Calculate the volume V G of the glass of the test-tube using the equation V G = ( V 2 – V 1 ). V G = ...................................................... [2]

parts.label: c
parts.text: (c) The student removes the test-tube from the measuring cylinder and empties the water back into the measuring cylinder. He then puts the test-tube, open end first, into the water in the measuring cylinder and carefully pushes it down with his finger until it is covered with water as shown in Fig. 5.3. Fig. 5.3

parts.label: iii
parts.text: (iii) Calculate the volume V A of air in the test-tube using the equation V A = ( V 3 – V 1 ) – V G . V A = ...................................................... [1]
